summary: Meta announced Muse Spark 1.1, an updated multimodal reasoning model with improved agentic, coding and tool-use capabilities, alongside a public preview of a new Meta Model API for developer access.

mechanisms.reason: The model is stated to actively manage a one-million-token context window, increasing memory content required per session.
mechanisms.quote: Muse Spark 1.1 can actively manage its context window of 1 million tokens.

mechanisms.reason: The model is designed to orchestrate multi-agent systems with parallel subagents, implying more calls issued per task.
mechanisms.quote: it is trained to orchestrate multi-agent systems to optimize end-to-end latency. As the main agent, it can gather context, make a plan, and delegate execution across parallel subagents.

mechanisms.reason: The release is explicitly built around agents performing delegated real-world tasks (computer use, marketplace listings, dinner orders) rather than a human operating software directly.
mechanisms.quote: Muse Spark 1.1 delivers exceptional performance in personal agentic tasks that require planning and orchestration across a range of external apps and services.

practices.reason: The model is claimed to improve substantially on tool/computer use, coding, and multimodal understanding, but the comparisons are the lab's own internal and partner testimony, unreplicated externally.
practices.quote: Muse Spark 1.1 is a multimodal reasoning model built for agentic tasks, with major gains in tool and computer use, coding, and multimodal understanding.

practices.reason: Meta describes its own internal safety and coding evaluation frameworks and thresholds, but these are lab-internal and not directly transferable to an external team's testing pipeline.
practices.quote: We conducted extensive safety evaluations before deployment, following the Advanced AI Scaling Framework , which defines evaluations, threat models, and deployment thresholds for our most advanced models.

practices.reason: A new API surface is being opened for developer access, requiring integration work to build against it.
practices.quote: For the first time, developers can begin building with Muse Spark 1.1 via the new Meta Model API, now in public preview.

practices.reason: The model exposes concrete agentic scaffolding features (planning mode, subagent delegation, context compaction) that a team could design pipelines around, though details are tied to Meta's own harness support.
practices.quote: Muse Spark 1.1 performs well with popular agentic coding setups, supporting common features like planning mode, goal conditioning, subagent delegation, and context compaction.
